discovery: Fluctuation theorems and exact nonequilibrium work relations

nominees.name: Christopher Jarzynski
nominees.affiliation: University of Maryland, College Park, USA

nominees.name: Giovanni Gallavotti
nominees.affiliation: Sapienza University of Rome and INFN, Italy

subfield: Statistical physics / nonequilibrium and quantum thermodynamics
motivation: For the discovery of fluctuation theorems, exact relations that hold arbitrarily far from equilibrium. Evans, Cohen and Searles first found the steady-state fluctuation relation in simulations, and Gallavotti and Cohen proved it for chaotic dynamics. Jarzynski's equality then linked irreversible work to equilibrium free energies. Together these results turned the second law from an inequality on averages into exact statements about the full statistics of entropy production. They have been confirmed in single-molecule pulling, colloidal particles, single-electron boxes and electronic circuits. Their quantum extensions now underlie full-counting statistics of charge and heat in mesoscopic conductors. They are the foundation of stochastic and quantum thermodynamics, including thermodynamic uncertainty relations and fundamental precision-dissipation bounds for nanoscale engines, clocks and quantum devices. The relations are universal across platforms and have been verified experimentally. This work rewrote how physicists understand irreversibility at small scales.
